note: This question evolved gradually within chess theory rather than being formally posed at a single moment. Early discussion appears in 1786 (Traité des Amateurs) debating whether perfect play yields a draw. Wilhelm Steinitz formalized the draw hypothesis in 1889. Claude Shannon outlined the theoretical procedure for perfect play in 1950. The question's origins predate modern formalization but lack a single documented inception date.
